items.h1: GPS Tracking & Fleet Management in Kenya
items.hero_text: Track trucks, matatus, delivery vans, motorcycles and company cars across Kenya with live location, fuel monitoring and driver safety tools from ITrackZen.
items.snapshot: Kenya is East Africa's busiest freight gateway. Cargo leaves the port of Mombasa for Nairobi and continues along the Northern Corridor towards Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and eastern DR Congo, while Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu and Nakuru run dense passenger, courier and boda boda networks. A tracking setup for Kenya usually has to cover long-haul visibility and congested city operations at the same time.
items.corridors: Mombasa to Nairobi, then onwards on the Northern Corridor to Malaba and Busia and into Uganda.

use_cases.title: Port-to-inland haulage
use_cases.text: Follow containers and bulk cargo from Mombasa, set geofences around yards and depots, and measure dwell time and turnaround.

use_cases.title: Matatu and bus operators
use_cases.text: Monitor speed, route adherence and driver behaviour for passenger service vehicles, with alerts that reach supervisors straight away.

use_cases.title: Courier and boda boda delivery
use_cases.text: Use compact trackers on motorcycles and vans to see where each rider is and to review completed delivery routes.

use_cases.title: Construction and project fleets
use_cases.text: Control fuel use and after-hours movement of tippers, lorries and plant across sites in and around Nairobi.

items.connectivity: Trackers need a data SIM from a local mobile network such as Safaricom, Airtel or Telkom. Coverage is strong along major roads and in towns and weaker in remote northern and border areas, where devices store positions and upload them when signal returns.

steps.title: Choose your hardware path
steps.text: Use trackers you already own if their model is supported, or ask us to recommend OBD, hardwired, motorcycle or dashcam devices.

steps.title: Request a quote
steps.text: Tell us your vehicle count and routes. We confirm device compatibility, plan and how hardware supply and installation can be arranged for your location.

steps.title: Activate and monitor
steps.text: Once your devices report to the platform, you sign in at itrackzen.com on web or mobile and set your alerts.

conditions: Hardware supply and installation availability is confirmed during your quote, not assumed.
Tracking depends on mobile data coverage and an active SIM plan on each device.
Fuel monitoring needs a compatible tracker and a fuel sensor, installed and calibrated.
items.partners: We are interested in hearing from Kenyan logistics operators, vehicle dealers, security firms and installers who want to offer ITrackZen to their own customers, and from corporate fleets that want a joint pilot.

faq.q: Can I track vehicles that cross into Uganda?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the tracker has data coverage. Many fleets use a SIM that supports roaming or a regional data plan. Tell us your routes when you request a quote.

faq.q: Do you support motorcycle trackers for boda boda fleets?
faq.a: Compact motorcycle trackers are among the supported device types. Compatibility depends on the exact model, so check the Supported GPS Trackers page or ask us.

items.h1: GPS Tracking & Fleet Management in Uganda
items.hero_text: GPS tracking for Uganda: real-time vehicle tracking for trucks in transit, buses, courier vans and boda boda fleets, with fuel and driver monitoring from ITrackZen.
items.snapshot: Uganda is landlocked, so most imports and exports travel hundreds of kilometres by road from Mombasa or Dar es Salaam. At the same time Kampala and its surrounding towns depend on boda boda motorcycles, taxis and delivery vans. Fleet operators here need visibility on long transit legs and discipline in dense city traffic.
items.corridors: Northern Corridor via Malaba and Busia, the Kampala to Gulu and Elegu route towards South Sudan, and western routes towards Rwanda and DR Congo.

use_cases.title: Transit and cross-border trucks
use_cases.text: See where each truck is between border posts and your depot, and use border and warehouse geofences to track waiting times.

use_cases.title: Boda boda and rider fleets
use_cases.text: Install small, tamper-resistant trackers on motorcycles to check routes, stops and after-hours use for rider-based businesses.

use_cases.title: NGO and project vehicles
use_cases.text: Give programme managers a clear record of trips, mileage and fuel for vehicles working in different districts.

use_cases.title: Bus and staff transport
use_cases.text: Monitor speed and route compliance for school, staff and long-distance coach services.

items.connectivity: Trackers need a data SIM from a local network such as MTN Uganda or Airtel Uganda. Coverage is good around Kampala and main highways, and reduced in some rural areas and national parks.

steps.title: Pick the right device

steps.title: Send an enquiry

steps.title: Go live

conditions: Installation capacity in Uganda is confirmed per request. We do not assume local installation teams.
A data SIM with credit is required in every tracker.
Features such as fuel monitoring or engine cut-off depend on device model and correct installation.
items.partners: Ugandan transport companies, vehicle importers, security companies and electronics installers are welcome to contact us about reseller and installation partnerships, as are corporate fleets interested in a trial.

faq.q: Can I track boda boda motorcycles?
faq.a: Yes, compact motorcycle trackers are supported. Choose a model from the supported list or ask us to check one you already own.

faq.q: Is tracking possible on the Northern Corridor?
faq.a: Tracking works wherever the device has mobile data. Positions are stored on the tracker during signal gaps and uploaded when it reconnects.

items.h1: GPS Tracking & Fleet Management in Ethiopia
items.hero_text: Vehicle tracking and fleet management for Ethiopia: follow trucks on the Djibouti corridor, manage company fleets and add fuel, driver and camera monitoring with ITrackZen.
items.snapshot: Ethiopia has no coastline, and most foreign trade moves by road between Addis Ababa and the port of Djibouti through Adama and Dire Dawa. This makes freight visibility, fuel control and driver monitoring especially valuable for transport and logistics companies, while Addis Ababa fleets need tools for staff transport, ride services and delivery.
items.corridors: The Addis Ababa, Adama, Dire Dawa and Djibouti corridor, plus routes towards Hawassa in the south and the northern regions.

use_cases.title: Import and export freight
use_cases.text: Track trucks between the port, dry ports and warehouses, review stops and measure round-trip times.

use_cases.title: Fuel and cargo tankers
use_cases.text: Where compatible sensors are fitted, monitor fuel level and unusual drops, and restrict vehicles to approved routes.

use_cases.title: Staff and school transport
use_cases.text: Give transport managers live location, speed alerts and trip history for buses and minibuses.

use_cases.title: Ride and delivery services
use_cases.text: Use trip history and driver ID to settle disputes and keep service quality consistent.

items.connectivity: Trackers need a data SIM from a local operator such as Ethio Telecom or Safaricom Ethiopia. Network availability and import rules for electronic devices can affect how quickly hardware can be supplied, so we confirm both during the quote.

steps.title: Check your devices
steps.text: Share the models you already use or describe your vehicles, and we confirm which trackers fit.

steps.title: Request a quote

steps.title: Start monitoring
steps.text: Sign in to the platform at itrackzen.com when your devices are reporting.

conditions: Customs, import and installation arrangements are confirmed per request.
Data coverage and SIM availability influence how well a tracker reports on remote stretches.
Camera and video features depend on the specific dashcam model and network bandwidth.
items.partners: We welcome enquiries from Ethiopian logistics firms, vehicle technology resellers and corporate fleets that would like to cooperate or pilot ITrackZen, subject to local requirements.

faq.q: Can ITrackZen follow trucks to Djibouti?
faq.a: Yes, tracking continues across borders as long as the device has data coverage. A cross-border data plan is recommended; we can advise when you request a quote.

faq.q: Can I use a tracker I already have?
faq.a: Very likely if it uses a supported protocol. Send us the model and we will confirm.

items.h1: GPS Tracking & Fleet Management in Somalia
items.hero_text: GPS tracking for Somalia: live vehicle tracking, geofencing, SOS alerts and reports for transport, security and humanitarian fleets, with ITrackZen.
items.snapshot: Operating vehicles in Somalia means long distances, varied road conditions and a strong need to know where drivers and cargo are. Ports at Mogadishu, Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo feed inland trucking, while security companies, NGOs and fuel distributors depend on dependable location data and fast alerts.
items.corridors: Port-to-city and inter-regional routes, including links from Berbera towards Hargeisa and Ethiopia.

use_cases.title: Trucking from the ports
use_cases.text: Follow cargo leaving Mogadishu, Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo and review stops, speed and route history.

use_cases.title: Security and escort vehicles
use_cases.text: Use SOS alerts, geofenced zones and live location to coordinate patrols and escorts from a control room.

use_cases.title: Humanitarian and project fleets
use_cases.text: Keep an auditable record of trips, mileage and fuel for vehicles serving programmes in different regions.

use_cases.title: Fuel distribution
use_cases.text: Monitor tanker routes and, with compatible sensors, fuel level and unusual drops.

items.connectivity: Trackers need a data SIM from a local mobile operator such as Hormuud, Telesom or Golis, and coverage varies by region. Devices keep positions in memory when signal is lost and upload them once they reconnect.

steps.title: Describe your operation
steps.text: Tell us your vehicle types, regions and what must be monitored.

steps.title: Get a quote
steps.text: We confirm supported hardware and discuss how supply and installation can be arranged for your location before any commitment.

steps.title: Activate and track
steps.text: Sign in at itrackzen.com on web or mobile when your trackers report.

conditions: We do not assume local installers or stock in Somalia. Supply and installation are confirmed in each quote.
Real-time tracking needs mobile data coverage; remote areas may report with delay.
Sensitive operations should use appropriate hardware concealment and access control, which we can discuss.
items.partners: Somali transport companies, security firms and technology resellers can contact us about installation and reseller partnerships, and about corporate cooperation.

faq.q: Does tracking work without a signal?
faq.a: The tracker records positions while offline and sends them when coverage returns, so your route history stays complete, although live updates pause during the gap.

faq.q: Can drivers send an emergency alert?
faq.a: Where the tracker has a panic or SOS input and a button is installed, an SOS event can raise an alert in the platform.

items.snapshot: Supplies for Juba and other South Sudanese centres travel long distances from Uganda and Kenya, often over roads that become difficult in the rainy season. Fleets in this setting benefit from reliable route history, geofenced safe zones, fuel control and clear records for donors and partners.
items.corridors: Routes from Uganda through Elegu and Nimule to Juba, and from Kenya towards Juba, with onward legs to regional towns.

use_cases.title: Humanitarian and NGO logistics
use_cases.text: Provide trip logs, mileage and fuel records that support programme reporting and accountability.

use_cases.title: Long-haul supply trucks

use_cases.title: Project and construction vehicles

use_cases.title: Security and escort teams
use_cases.text: Coordinate vehicles with live location and SOS alerts.

items.connectivity: Mobile networks such as MTN and Zain operate in main towns, and coverage thins quickly outside them. Trackers buffer data offline, but live visibility depends on signal, so plan routes and SIM options with us.

items.h1: GPS Tracking & Fleet Management in DR Congo
items.hero_text: GPS tracking for DR Congo: monitor trucks, buses and project vehicles across vast distances with live location, fuel control and reports from ITrackZen.
items.snapshot: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is vast, and its freight routes from Lubumbashi and Kolwezi to southern Africa and East African ports cover long, demanding distances. Fleets also operate in and around Kinshasa, Goma and Kisangani. Accurate tracking, fuel control and maintenance planning matter when vehicles are far from workshops.
items.corridors: Routes from the Katanga mining region through Kasumbalesa and onward, links from Goma towards Uganda and Rwanda, and the Matadi to Kinshasa road.

use_cases.title: Mining and heavy haulage
use_cases.text: Track haul trucks and convoys, monitor stops and idle time and schedule maintenance by distance or engine hours.

use_cases.title: Cross-border freight
use_cases.text: Follow cargo from Lubumbashi towards Zambia and beyond, with border geofences and dwell-time reports.

use_cases.title: Project and NGO vehicles
use_cases.text: Keep trip and fuel records for vehicles spread across provinces.

use_cases.title: Urban fleets
use_cases.text: Use fleet dashboards for staff transport, taxis and delivery in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi.

items.connectivity: Networks such as Vodacom, Airtel, Orange and Africell cover cities and main routes, while large rural areas have little or no coverage. Devices store data offline and upload it when they reconnect, and satellite-capable options can be discussed for critical assets.

items.partners: We welcome contact from Congolese transport and mining-services companies, technology resellers, installers and corporate fleets interested in cooperation.

faq.q: Is tracking possible in areas with poor coverage?
faq.a: A tracker can log positions without signal and upload them when it reconnects. Real-time visibility depends on coverage.

faq.q: Can you help plan maintenance for heavy trucks?
faq.a: Maintenance reminders can be based on distance, engine hours or dates, where the device reports the needed data.
